evidence: The guard argv in engine/review/claudeprint/claudeprint.go is `--print --output-format text --tools "" --permission-mode dontAsk --no-session-persistence --setting-sources "" --model <model> --system-prompt <fixed text>`. The command is exec'd directly with no shell, so the empty arguments are passed as given. TestReviewRunsClaudePrintWithNoToolsInTheWorktreeAndAnswersItsStdout pins this exact slice with reflect.DeepEqual, so dropping or changing any guard flag fails that test. The cmd-level test only checks a prefix, and the claudeprint test covers the rest.

Stdin is the agent-file body, a blank line, the brief, then the frozen context. In engine/review/app/launch.go, `CheckBrief` and the size limit run before `withContext` and before `s.reviewer.Review`, so every refusal happens before claude starts. A missing or foreign agent file is refused before the runner is called, and the tests assert `calls == 0`.

Working directory: `Review` passes `bound.Worktree` to `OutputStdinIn`, which sets `cmd.Dir`. An empty dir keeps the old behaviour, so the existing `Output` and `OutputStdin` paths are unchanged. The execrunner test covers the new method.
Environment: `d.environment()` is passed whole, as the codex adapter already does. No new exposure is introduced.

Failure paths: a non-zero exit, a deadline, and empty or whitespace-only stdout all wrap `ErrReviewerDidNotAnswer`, and the tests cover each. Stderr is bounded to 2000 bytes, and the agent file read is bounded to 1 MiB.

`ClaudeInstructions` matches the writer at engine/agentgen/roles.go:257. The writer emits `---
name: ..
description: ..
model: ..
tools: ..
---

` followed by the body, and the parser expects exactly that. A per-role test checks that the body equals the Codex body.

Not proven by any test, and the package comment says so: whether the installed claude honours `--tools ""` and `--setting-sources ""`, and whether MCP tools or the candidate's CLAUDE.md are reachable. With `dontAsk` and no loaded allow rules, unapproved tools should be denied. I have no concrete proof of a defect here, so I report nothing for it.
